subject: Hosted API: data locality, retention windows and deletion flow — security responses
messages:

Cc: security@novumhealth.com

Subject: Data residency & retention Qs for Hosted API (Novum)

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the call this morning. As we discussed, our security review team needs concise answers to the attached questionnaire focused on three areas: (1) where customer data is stored (residency), (2) default retention windows and what can be configured, and (3) the deletion/erasures process (including backups).

Highlights we care about: we need an explicit SLA for deletions once requested, confirmation that EU data stays within EU if we choose that option, and evidence of how backups are handled during purge. Can you return a short response we can include in our vendor assessment?

I've attached the questionnaire and a simplified dataflow diagram.

Best,
Sara Patel
Security Engineering Manager
Novum Health

Attachments: Novum_Security_Q3_2029_SQ.pdf (PDF, 1 page); novum-dataflow-simplified.png (PNG, 96KB)

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Patel <sara.patel@novumhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 02 Apr 2029 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data residency & retention Qs for Hosted API (Novum)

Sara —

Appreciate the clear list. Below is a compact response pack you can paste into Novum's vendor assessment. I've also attached a short evidence bundle and a link to our region-routing matrix. If you want us to move Novum's tenancy to EU-only, we can set that up as part of onboarding (requires region selection and a short cutover window).

1) Data residency (where customer data is stored)
- Default: multi-region (primary region selected at account creation). For US-based accounts we host customer request/response payloads and logs in US regions.
- EU-only option: available for customers who require data to remain in EU; we deploy tenant data stores and request routing in EU (eu-central/1). This is available during onboarding or as a migration (coordination required).
- Model weights and third-party model artifacts are not customer-specific and remain in global model stores; customer content is isolated from model artifacts.

2) Retention windows (defaults and configuration)
- Request/response content (raw prompt + generated output): retained 30 days by default for billing, abuse detection, and debugging. Customer may reduce this to 0 days (ephemeral) on request; this is implemented as a tenancy flag that prevents any persistent storage of payloads beyond transient caches.
- Request metadata (timestamps, rate metrics): retained 90 days for operational analytics; customers can request retention reduction for compliance reasons (case-by-case).
- Short-term KV/prefix cache: ephemeral (default TTL 1 hour) and only stored in-memory or local node SSDs; not replicated to long-term object stores.
- Aggregated telemetry and usage metrics: stored for 13 months to support product and billing analysis (can be excluded for enterprise contracts).

3) Deletion / erasure flow (how we remove data)
- Customer-facing API: we provide an erase endpoint and a support-assisted erasure request. Once an erase request is submitted the system marks records for deletion (soft-delete) immediately.
- Purge schedule: a background job runs continuous purges; primary deletion completes within 72 hours of request for live stores.
- Backups & replicas: snapshots are rotated; any snapshots containing subject data are marked and purged on the next scheduled snapshot rotation. For forensic integrity we retain immutable backups for up to 90 days by default, but data in those backups is inaccessible via normal reads and will be cryptographically shredded when we perform backup-level purges (we provide attestation on request).
- Verification: we provide a deletion confirmation report for the erasure request (timestamped). For high-compliance customers we can arrange additional attestation (SOC2 scope) as part of the contract.

4) Access controls and logging
- Tenant isolation: logical separation via our tenancy abstraction; customer data is accessible only by authorized services and account-level roles.
- Audit logs: admin-level access to erasure operations is recorded and retained for 12 months.

5) Controls for debugging and human review
- By default, Redwood does not surface customer content to human reviewers. If Novum requests troubleshooting that requires content access, Redwood will only do so with advance authorization and a temporary access token logged in the audit trail.

Next steps: I can (a) drop Novum into an EU-only tenant preview if you'd like, and (b) attach the deletion attestation template we use for enterprise SLAs. Let me know which you'd prefer.

Thanks,

Thanks Naomi — this is helpful and mostly aligned with what we need. A couple clarifying items before we close the questionnaire:

1) For the 0-day option (ephemeral payloads), can you confirm whether any asynchronous logs (error traces, sampling traces) might still contain extracted text? We need to ensure PII is not persisted elsewhere.

2) For backups: you mentioned cryptographic shredding on purge — can you provide a short explanation of the process / how we would verify?

If you can reply to those two points we can finalize and move to procurement.

Best,
Sara

On the attachments: the questionnaire is the single-page PDF we attached; we may add a brief note to procurement referencing the deletion attestation for contract language.

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Data residency & retention Qs for Hosted API (Novum)

Sara — quick follow-up from infra/security on the two clarifications: we can confirm the following and we will include both items in the attestation bundle.

1) Ephemeral mode and async logs:
- Behavior: when a tenancy flag is set to 0-day retention, all runtime components operate in ephemeral mode. Error traces generated by edge services are redacted at source (we redact payloads greater than 32 bytes and replace with hashed digests in logs). Application-level sampling for debugging is disabled by default; when temporarily enabled it follows strict redaction policies and requires explicit customer consent.

2) Backup cryptographic shredding process:
- Process summary: backups are encrypted with tenant-specific envelope keys. When a purge request requires removal from backups, we rotate the envelope key and zeroize the old key material. Without the envelope key the ciphertext is unrecoverable. Our operations team records a key-rotation and zeroization event; we can provide a signed attestation and the key-rotation event id.
- Verification: we can provide the rotation event id and the retention window that confirmed the old snapshots were re-encrypted or retired; for contract-level requirements we include a timeline in the attestation.

If Novum would like formal language for procurement we can draft a 2-paragraph contract addendum describing the 0-day option, 72-hour purge SLA, and the backup key-rotation attestation.

Regards,
Irene Choi
Principal, Infrastructure Security
Redwood Inference
